_comment_top: NimRTC vendor manifest. Locks every third-party dependency to a specific commit/tag/SHA so reproducible builds are possible without 280+ MB of vendored source. See docs/plan/vendor-migration.md.

policy._comment_policy: Submodules with pinned SHAs are the source of truth. This file is read by tools/check_vendor.py to verify local submodules match. Update by running `python tools/vendor_update.py <name>`.

vendors.name: wolfssl
vendors.notes: DTLS production backend. Submodule path is /src because CMakeLists.txt add_subdirectory(src wolfssl_build) is the layout wolfSSL ships.

vendors.name: webrtc_audio_processing
vendors.build: external (Meson) — see tools/build_webrtc_apm.{cmd,sh}; CMake only consumes pre-built artifacts under build_meson/
vendors.notes: WebRTC APM. Built out-of-tree via Meson (not CMake) because upstream is Meson-first. The source tree is NOT vendored into git: it is cloned at build time by tools/fetch_webrtc_apm.py and patched by tools/apply_webrtc_apm_patches.py. NimRTC's changes to the upstream tree live as versioned patches in src/third_party/webrtc_audio_processing/patches/ (currently 0001-cxx20.patch, which raises the Meson build to C++20 — required by agc2/*.cc). Because the tree is fetched rather than committed, this vendor has NO .gitmodules entry and NO gitlink in the index — 'submodule_path' here names the on-disk location that tools/check_vendor.py inspects, not a registered submodule. After clone, run tools/build_webrtc_apm.sh (Linux/macOS) or tools/build_webrtc_apm.cmd (Windows).

vendors.name: mbedtls
vendors.build: HISTORICAL ONLY — DTLS production path migrated to wolfSSL. CMake wrapper at src/third_party/mbedtls/CMakeLists.txt only exposes headers via INTERFACE.
vendors.notes: No longer linked into nimrtc_dtls. Retained as archival source per CHANGELOG.md [0.9.0-rc1] Deferred-for-1.0 note; full removal is its own PR. NOT yet a submodule: the sources are still checked into this repository (vendor-migration.md Phase 3 pending). The checked-in tree is NOT byte-identical to the pinned revision, because upstream keeps its test framework in a separate 'framework' submodule whose contents are inlined here (2039 tracked files versus 332 upstream entries). A conversion therefore has to decide how to carry the inlined framework tree.

vendors.name: libjuice
vendors.notes: ICE transport. NOT yet a submodule: the sources are still checked into this repository (vendor-migration.md Phase 3 pending), so commit_sha pins the upstream revision the tree was taken from rather than the tree itself. The tree carries one NimRTC-local patch on top of that revision: src/third_party/libjuice/patches/0001-so-reuseaddr.patch. It does two things: (1) src/udp.c no longer sets SO_REUSEADDR/SO_REUSEPORT, so two ICE agents can never end up sharing one UDP port (the old setting let a second bind succeed, and also made the kernel ephemeral allocator hand out duplicate ports); (2) src/conn_mux.c refuses to merge an ephemeral-port (port_begin == 0 && port_end == 0) request into an existing mux registry, so two agents in one process no longer share a single socket and candidate. Converting it to a submodule requires that patch to be preserved (fork or versioned patch file) first.

vendors.name: libsrtp
vendors.notes: SRTP crypto with CRYPTO_LIBRARY=internal. Converted to a real submodule (vendor-migration.md Phase 3): the previously checked-in tree was byte-identical to the pinned revision, so no NimRTC-local patch had to be carried over. The index holds a gitlink at 160000; run `git submodule update --init src/third_party/libsrtp/src` to fetch.

vendors.name: googletest
vendors.notes: Test framework. Submodule root contains googletest/ and googlemock/ directories. v1.12.0 used because v1.12.1 was never tagged upstream.

vendors.name: nlohmann_json
vendors.build: Single-header INTERFACE library — only the header is needed.
vendors.notes: Single-header JSON. Submodule root has single_include/nlohmann/json.hpp; CMakeLists.txt wraps it as nlohmann_json::nlohmann_json.

vendors.name: gmssl
vendors.build: sources compiled directly via src/third_party/gmssl/CMakeLists.txt wrapper into STATIC nimrtc_vendor_gmssl — active only when NIMRTC_ENABLE_DTLS_GMSSL=ON (default OFF)
vendors.notes: GM/T crypto backend for DTLS/TLCP (v1.1 X1, ADR-013 correction). LICENSE verified 2026-11-05: upstream LICENSE is Apache-2.0, compatible with Apache-2.0. Converted to a real submodule pinned at v3.2.0; the index holds a gitlink at 160000; run `git submodule update --init src/third_party/gmssl/src` to fetch. Default build is unaffected (OFF → empty INTERFACE stub, zero compile-time/size cost). ON compiles the upstream default source set into STATIC nimrtc_vendor_gmssl (no add_subdirectory into upstream: upstream registers ctest entries unconditionally and CMake function shadowing is global, so entering it would break the tree). Windows/MSVC acceptance is the CI opt-in leg (see .github/workflows/ci.yml gmssl-vendored).

vendors.name: msquic
vendors.notes: WebTransport / QUIC backend for IWebTransportSession. Source populated by git submodule; CMakeLists.txt wraps the upstream src/CMakeLists.txt and exposes nimrtc_vendor_msquic. ADR-014 Criterion 5 (active maintenance: < 180 days) is verified at build time by interop/v0_14_msquic_spike/ CMake scripts. If criterion 5 fails, ADR-014 reopens and the fallback is quiche (BSD-2, C API). Last upstream commit: 2026-10-16 (3 days ago as of 2026-10-19). The submodule tracks the NimRTC fork, whose 'nimrtc-patches' branch is upstream 42376ae plus one NimRTC commit (a5ae3a06) that forces the dummy raw datapath on Windows, because the xdp-for-windows SDK is absent in the CI build environment. The pin is pushed to github.com/NimRTC/msquic, so it is fetchable from a fresh clone.

vendors.name: nv_codec_headers
vendors.notes: NVIDIA Video Codec SDK headers (nvEncodeAPI.h for NVENC, plus the nvcuvid / CUVID and FFmpeg-style dynamic-loader headers used by the NVDEC decoder). MIT-licensed: the headers are NVIDIA's own, redistributed by the FFmpeg project under the MIT licence, with the notice embedded in every file. NOT a submodule: the headers are checked into this repository rather than fetched, because they pin the struct ABI the NVENC / NVDEC backends build against — a submodule would allow the pin to drift away from the headers actually compiled, and the whole point of the vendored copy is that the struct layouts and the struct-version words come from the same header set (see README.md next to the headers and docs/hw_plugin_seam.md §12.1). 'submodule': false tells tools/check_vendor.py that this is a checked-in tree, so the manifest SHA documents the upstream revision it was taken from rather than describing the tree itself. No NVIDIA binary is linked or shipped: the backends load nvEncodeAPI64.dll / nvcuvid.dll / nvcuda.dll from the installed driver at runtime.

vendors.name: openh264
vendors.build: sources compiled directly via src/third_party/openh264/CMakeLists.txt wrapper into STATIC nimrtc_vendor_openh264 — active only when NIMRTC_PLUGINS_OPENH264=ON (default OFF)
vendors.notes: Real software H.264 encoder + decoder (remote-desktop plan WP-B, CPU bring-up baseline). Replaces the stub delegation in src/modules/h264/src/openh264_encoder.cpp with a genuine WelsCreateSVCEncoder / WelsCreateDecoder implementation; the stub survives as the fallback backend and reports backend_id() == "software-stub", while this one reports "openh264". Upstream ships a Meson build, so the wrapper compiles the upstream sources directly with CMake. The wrapper builds the PORTABLE C/C++ path only (X86_ASM and HAVE_NEON stay undefined), because upstream's x86 fast paths are NASM and its ARM paths are GAS — neither assembler is guaranteed on a NimRTC build host. The result is a correct, if slower, codec, which is exactly what the software baseline needs. No system codec library is linked (L5).

vendors.name: dav1d
vendors.build: sources compiled directly via src/third_party/dav1d/CMakeLists.txt wrapper into STATIC nimrtc_vendor_dav1d — active only when NIMRTC_PLUGINS_DAV1D=ON (default OFF)
vendors.notes: Real software AV1 decoder (remote-desktop plan WP-B, CPU bring-up baseline). Backs src/modules/av1/src/dav1d_decoder.cpp, which reports backend_id() == "dav1d"; the AV1 stub stays the fallback and reports "software-stub". Upstream ships a Meson build, so the wrapper compiles the upstream sources directly with CMake and reproduces the three things a naive source list would miss: (1) the generated config.h platform description, (2) the generated vcs_version.h, (3) the per-bitdepth instantiation of the templated DSP sources (*_tmpl.c) — here the 8-bit one only, in a separate OBJECT library so -DBITDEPTH=8 does not leak into the non-templated sources. Portable C path only (HAVE_ASM=0): upstream's x86 fast paths are NASM and its ARM ones are GAS, neither of which is guaranteed on a NimRTC build host. No system codec library is linked (L5).

vendors.name: libyuv
vendors.build: add_subdirectory(src) — see src/third_party/libyuv/CMakeLists.txt (upstream CMake, static `yuv` target re-exported as nimrtc_vendor_libyuv) — active whenever NIMRTC_VENDORED_LIBYUV=ON (default ON)
vendors.notes: YUV/RGB scale + convert library (remote-desktop plan C1, Track C 'Pixel'). The cross-platform default the plan names under RD-10: one implementation covers every platform NimRTC ships, with SSSE3 + AVX2 on x86-64 and NEON / SVE2 / SME on arm64. BSD-3-Clause, so it clears the RD-2 licence filter. Upstream ships its own CMakeLists.txt, so the wrapper adds it with BUILD_SHARED_LIBS=OFF, UNIT_TEST=OFF and LIBYUV_DISABLE_JPEG=ON; the upstream static `yuv` archive is re-exported as nimrtc_vendor_libyuv (alias nimrtc::vendor::libyuv) with the upstream include dir as a SYSTEM include. Platform matrix (K8b): Windows (MSVC, x86-64, SSSE3/AVX2), macOS (arm64, NEON), Linux x86-64 (SSSE3/AVX2), Linux aarch64 (NEON/SVE2/SME), Android (arm64/x86, NEON/SSSE3), iOS (arm64, NEON). No system library is linked (L5): the whole point is that every platform gets the SAME scale output (the plan's 'same-result check').

vendors.name: portaudio
vendors.build: sources compiled directly via src/third_party/portaudio/CMakeLists.txt wrapper into STATIC nimrtc_vendor_portaudio — active whenever NIMRTC_VENDORED_PORTAUDIO=ON (default ON)
vendors.notes: Cross-platform audio I/O (remote-desktop plan Track F, F2). ONE implementation covers every platform NimRTC ships, which is what RD-10 asks for — instead of three hand-written platform backends. The upstream tree ships its own stand-alone CMake build, so the wrapper compiles the upstream sources directly with CMake (the same pattern as openh264 / dav1d) and avoids entering upstream's project() / install() rules. Platform matrix (K8b): Windows (MSVC, x86-64) — WASAPI + MME (waveIn/waveOut) + DirectSound; macOS (arm64/x86-64) — Core Audio; Linux x86-64 — ALSA + PulseAudio, each enabled only when the build host carries the development package. ASIO is deliberately OFF (the Steinberg ASIO SDK may not be redistributed and upstream's CMake downloads it at configure time); WDM-KS and JACK are OFF for the same dependency reason. No system audio library is required: without any backend the library still compiles and PortAudio reports 'no host API' at runtime, so the module reports the device layer as unavailable rather than the build failing. MIT-licensed, so it clears the RD-2 licence filter.

vendors.name: libsamplerate
vendors.build: sources compiled directly via src/third_party/libsamplerate/CMakeLists.txt wrapper into STATIC nimrtc_vendor_libsamplerate — active whenever NIMRTC_VENDORED_LIBSAMPLERATE=ON (default ON)
vendors.notes: Sample-rate conversion (remote-desktop plan Track F, F5). The plan's Q-1 decision: a resampler is IN scope (a 44.1 kHz capture device is the common case, and pushing 'the host must convert' onto every consumer is not a decision), and libsamplerate is the implementation — BSD-2-Clause, cross-platform, actively maintained, with a CMake build upstream (chosen over SpeexDSP, whose resampler is BSD-3 but whose last release was 2022-06 and which has therefore been unmaintained since). Upstream ships its own stand-alone CMake project build, so the wrapper compiles the four upstream translation units (samplerate.c, src_linear.c, src_sinc.c, src_zoh.c) directly with CMake and generates the config.h the sources require — the same pattern as openh264 / dav1d / PortAudio. LICENCE: BSD-2-Clause (the upstream COPYING file, Copyright (c) 2012-2016 Erik de Castro Lopo), so it clears the plan's RD-2 licence filter. PLATFORM MATRIX (policy K8b) — libsamplerate is pure C99 over <math.h> with NO platform-specific code, so the SAME four sources build on every platform NimRTC ships and the resampler's output is bit-comparable across them: Windows (MSVC, x86-64 — the SSE2 lrint fast path is selected automatically on x86-64); macOS (arm64 / x86-64); Linux x86-64 (links libm); Linux aarch64 (links libm — upstream is scalar C, with no NEON fast path, so the arm64 result matches the x86-64 one). The wrapper compiles the FAST and MEDIUM sinc converters and deliberately leaves the BEST converter out: its coefficient table (src/high_qual_coeffs.h) is a ~9 MB array of doubles that costs a great deal of compile time and memory for a converter a remote desktop never selects. No system samplerate library is linked under any configuration (L5): with NIMRTC_VENDORED_LIBSAMPLERATE=OFF the audio-device module compiles its pure-C++ linear-interpolation fallback and reports backend() == "linear" rather than silently linking a system libsamplerate.

vendors.name: svt-av1
vendors.build: upstream's own CMake project entered in a sanitised way via the src/third_party/svt-av1/CMakeLists.txt wrapper into STATIC nimrtc_vendor_svt_av1 — active only when NIMRTC_VENDORED_SVT_AV1=ON (default OFF)
vendors.notes: Real software AV1 ENCODER (remote-desktop plan WP-B / B11). The plan's selection table names SVT-AV1 as the only cross-platform software AV1 encoder that carries the screen-content tools (intra block copy, the --scm mode) a remote control needs; libaom is excluded by the plan for build cost and latency, and the hardware encoders (Track B5 / B5a / B6) are the primary path with SVT-AV1 as the CPU fallback. It backs src/modules/av1/src/svt_av1_encoder.cpp, which reports backend_id() == "svt-av1"; the AV1 stub stays the fallback and reports "software-stub". LICENCE: BSD-2-Clause Clear PLUS the AOM Patent License 1.0 (upstream LICENSE.md and PATENTS.md) — both notices are reproduced in the tree's NOTICE file. PLATFORM MATRIX (policy K8b) — upstream is portable C99 plus NASM assembly for the x86-64 fast paths, so the SAME sources build everywhere but the SPEED differs: Windows (MSVC, x86-64) — NASM is NOT guaranteed on the NimRTC CI image, and upstream's own CMakeLists.txt calls enable_language(ASM_NASM) unconditionally on x86, which would make the configure step FAIL without NASM. The wrapper therefore probes for NASM itself and sets upstream's COMPILE_C_ONLY=ON when it is absent, so the build degrades the speed and never the build (plan R-11); Windows (MSVC, arm64) — NASM is x86-only, so the portable C path is used unconditionally; macOS (arm64 / x86-64) — NASM via Homebrew is the fast path, and the portable C path is the fallback; Linux x86-64 — NASM is usually present (the fast path) and the portable C path is the fallback; Linux aarch64 — NASM is never applicable, so the portable C path is the only one and the encoder is correspondingly slower. The option defaults OFF precisely because the build cost and the licence surface (a patent licence, unlike the BSD-only peers) do not clear the plan's bar for a default-on dependency. No system codec library is linked under any configuration (L5): with NIMRTC_VENDORED_SVT_AV1=OFF the AV1 backend table simply has no svt-av1 row.

vendors.name: libvpx
vendors.build: upstream translation units compiled directly via the src/third_party/libvpx/CMakeLists.txt wrapper into STATIC nimrtc_vendor_libvpx — active only when NIMRTC_VENDORED_LIBVPX=ON (default OFF)
vendors.notes: Real software VP9 codec (remote-desktop plan WP-B / B11). B11 asks for an optional software VP9 encoder behind NIMRTC_VENDORED_LIBVPX, which defaults OFF. libvpx is the reference VP9 implementation and the only one with a permissive licence (BSD-3-Clause) that clears the plan's RD-2 licence filter. It backs src/modules/vp9/src/libvpx_vp9_codec.cpp, which reports backend_id() == "libvpx"; the VP9 software stub stays the fallback and reports "software-stub". WHY A HAND-WRITTEN WRAPPER: upstream libvpx ships a hand-rolled `configure` script (borrowed from FFmpeg) rather than a CMake project, and its build additionally depends on perl (the rtcd.pl dispatch-table generators, whose outputs are NOT checked in) and on make. The wrapper compiles the upstream translation units directly with CMake (the same pattern as openh264 / dav1d) and pre-generates the rtcd.c tables with perl at configure time, which removes the make dependency entirely. LICENCE: BSD-3-Clause (upstream LICENSE, Copyright (c) 2010-2023 The WebM Project), so it clears the plan's RD-2 licence filter. PLATFORM MATRIX (policy K8b) — upstream is portable C99 plus optional assembler fast paths, and the wrapper deliberately compiles the portable C path only (the upstream assembly is NASM on x86 and GAS on ARM, neither of which is guaranteed on a NimRTC build host), so the SAME sources build on every platform NimRTC ships: Windows (MSVC, x86-64 / arm64); macOS (arm64 / x86-64); Linux x86-64 (needs libm); Linux aarch64 (needs libm — upstream is scalar C, with no NEON fast path, so the arm64 output is bit-comparable with the x86-64 one). The perl dependency remains: without perl the wrapper degrades to an empty INTERFACE target and the VP9 row is simply ABSENT from the registry, rather than failing the configure step (plan R-11). The option defaults OFF. No system codec library is linked under any configuration (L5): with NIMRTC_VENDORED_LIBVPX=OFF the VP9 backend table has no libvpx row.

tools.name: tools/check_vendor.py
tools._comment: Verifies every submodule SHA matches this manifest. Wired into CI as warning-only gate.

tools.name: tools/vendor_update.py
tools._comment: Pulls a new upstream tag, updates the submodule, and rewrites vendor.json.

tools.name: tools/ci_preflight.py
tools._comment: Cross-platform pre-flight check for CMake ≥ 3.25 and required build tools.
